components.name: Accent Button
components.description: The one primary action per screen, such as Export video.
components.css: .ds-btn-accent { font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; font-weight: 600; height: 32px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid rgba(120, 70, 10, 0.22); background: #E8962E; color: #1F1404; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 83ms linear; } .ds-btn-accent:hover { background: #EEA444; } .ds-btn-accent:active { background: #D78722; color: #3A2508; } .ds-btn-accent:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #FEFDFC, 0 0 0 3px #1C1B19; }

components.name: Standard Button
components.description: Secondary actions such as Choose photos or Cancel export.
components.css: .ds-btn-standard { font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #DCDAD5; background: #FEFDFC; color: #1C1B19; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 83ms linear; } .ds-btn-standard:hover { background: #F6F5F3; } .ds-btn-standard:active { background: #F0EEEB; color: #5D5A55; } .ds-btn-standard:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #FEFDFC, 0 0 0 3px #1C1B19; }

components.name: Subtle Button
components.description: Command bar actions with an icon.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-subtle"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 3v10M3 8h10"/></svg>Add photos</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-subtle { font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid transparent; background: transparent; color: #1C1B19; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 83ms linear; } .ds-btn-subtle:hover { background: rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.06); } .ds-btn-subtle:active { background: rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.10); color: #5D5A55; } .ds-btn-subtle:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #FEFDFC, 0 0 0 3px #1C1B19; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Speed mode, speed value, shape and fit. The selected pill is neutral, never amber.
components.css: .ds-seg { font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); width: 280px; height: 32px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 2px; border-radius: 5px; background: #F0EEEB; border: 1px solid #DCDAD5; } .ds-seg button { font: inherit; font-size: 13px; border: 0; border-radius: 3px; background: transparent; color: #5D5A55; cursor: pointer; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: background-color 250ms cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1); } .ds-seg button:hover { color: #1C1B19; } .ds-seg button[aria-checked="true"] { background: #FEFDFC; color: #1C1B19; font-weight: 600; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.14), 0 0 0 1px rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.04); } .ds-seg button:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #FEFDFC, 0 0 0 3px #1C1B19; }

components.name: Toggle
components.description: On and off settings such as Deflicker and Reduce motion.
components.css: .ds-toggle { position: relative; width: 40px; height: 20px; padding: 0; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #5D5A55; background: transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 167ms linear, border-color 167ms linear; } .ds-toggle span { position: absolute; left: 3px; top: 3px; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; background: #5D5A55; transition: transform 167ms cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1); } .ds-toggle[aria-checked="true"] { background: #B5620D; border-color: #B5620D; } .ds-toggle[aria-checked="true"] span { background: #FEFDFC; transform: translateX(20px); } .ds-toggle:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #FEFDFC, 0 0 0 3px #1C1B19; }

components.name: Caution InfoBar
components.description: Floats over the preview: what happened, one action, dismiss.
components.html: 3 photos couldn't be read and were skipped.
components.css: .ds-infobar { font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; max-width: 560px; padding: 10px 8px 10px 14px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #DCDAD5; background: #FFF7DB; color: #1C1B19; box-shadow: 0 8px 28px rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.16), 0 2px 6px rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.06); } .ds-infobar span { flex: 1; } .ds-infobar button { font: inherit; font-size: 13px; height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #DCDAD5; background: #FEFDFC; color: #1C1B19; cursor: pointer; } .ds-infobar button:hover { background: #F6F5F3; } .ds-infobar button:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #FEFDFC, 0 0 0 3px #1C1B19; }

components.name: Filmstrip
components.description: Signature: thumbnails are buttons; the amber ring marks where the video is now.
components.css: .ds-film { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 64px); gap: 4px; padding: 6px; background: #FAF9F7; } .ds-film button { aspect-ratio: 3 / 2; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 3px; cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 167ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 167ms linear; } .ds-film button:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #FAF9F7, 0 0 0 3px #5D5A55; } .ds-film button[aria-current="true"] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #FAF9F7, 0 0 0 4px #B5620D; } .ds-film button.pending { opacity: 0.35; } .ds-film button:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #FAF9F7, 0 0 0 4px #1C1B19; }

narrative.overview:
10Lapse is the gate a sequence passes through on its way to becoming a film. The gate itself is plain, exact and native to Windows 11; everything with color belongs to the photos moving through it. The chrome is Fluent through and through: Mica behind the title and command bars, a single content layer for the stage and inspector, stock WinUI controls, Segoe UI Variable. It should feel like part of Windows, the way Photos or Snipping Tool do, and then disappear into the job of turning 742 photos into 24.7 seconds of sunset.

Density is calm. One window, one stage, one inspector with four sections (Timing, Frame, Output, Look), one accent button. Numbers are always on screen and always right, set in tabular figures. Light and dark get equal care and follow the Windows setting; high contrast maps every token to a system color.

Motion is cinematic when the user creates something and invisible the rest of the time. Choreography plays on import (the first frame develops like a print while thumbnails file into the strip), during export (frames pass an amber gate as they are encoded) and on finish (one quiet check, then the preview premieres the result). Nothing animates on launch, nothing blocks input, and every movement has a reduced-motion fallback that is a short fade.

This system rejects: the legacy 10Lapse 2.x UI (blurred background photo, three equal accent buttons, grey full-screen overlays, a "Policy!" wall of text on first run); generic SaaS dashboards (hero metrics, card grids, gradient washes); skeuomorphic camera apps (fake dials, film sprockets, leather textures); and pro editors' density.
keyCharacteristics: Native Windows 11 Fluent, one typeface, stock controls.
Neutral chrome warmed by a hair; the photos carry the color.
Golden-hour amber marks only the primary action, progress, the playhead and the selected frame.
Always-visible math: "742 photos → 24.7 s at 30 frames per second".
4 px grid, 32 px controls, 20 px stage and inspector padding, 16 px section rhythm.
Inspector docks right at 320 px from 1000 px wide; below that it folds into a 260 px tabbed panel under the preview; smallest window 640 × 480.

Motion tokens: Tap 83 ms, Control 167 ms, Reveal 250 ms, Scene 400 ms, Cinema 700 ms; Enter `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, Exit `cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)`, Move `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)`, linear for playback and progress.

rules.name: The Photos Are The Color Rule
rules.body: Chrome stays neutral. Amber covers well under a tenth of any screen, and only on the primary action, progress, the playhead and the selected frame.

rules.name: The Indicator Rule
rules.body: In light theme, anything that conveys state without text uses Deep Amber Indicator, never Golden Hour Amber.

rules.name: The Ramp Stays Outside Rule
rules.body: The day-to-night ramp never colors UI chrome or text. If a control is rose or dusk, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes (frame counters, time codes, speed, percent, file size) uses tabular figures, and frame numbers are zero-padded to the width of the total ("0312 of 0742").

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and buttons are sentence case and name the action: "Export video", "Cancel export", never "OK" or "Submit". No exclamation marks, no "Oops".

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: Only flyouts cast a shadow. Cards, panels and the inspector never do. If a settings row has a shadow, remove it.

dos: **Do** keep chrome neutral and let the photos carry the color (The Photos Are The Color Rule).
**Do** use Deep Amber Indicator (`#B5620D`) for every light-theme indicator; check 3:1 for indicators and 4.5:1 for text.
**Do** show photo count, speed and length together, in tabular figures, at all times.
**Do** use stock WinUI controls, Mica and the system title bar; familiar Windows patterns beat invented ones.
**Do** animate only transform, opacity, filter and clip-path, with the motion tokens, and give every animation a reduced-motion fade.
**Do** float InfoBars over the preview and say what happened and what to do next, with one action.
**Do** design light, dark and high contrast together; switching theme crossfades over 250 ms.
donts: **Don't** bring back the legacy 10Lapse 2.x UI: blurred background photo, three equal accent buttons, grey full-screen overlays, a "Policy!" wall of text on first run.
**Don't** look like a generic SaaS dashboard: hero metrics, card grids, gradient washes.
**Don't** go skeuomorphic: fake dials, film sprockets, leather textures.
**Don't** reach for pro editors' density (DaVinci Resolve, Premiere); 10Lapse has one job and a handful of controls.
**Don't** put more than one accent button on a screen, or use amber for a selected segment.
**Don't** use a modal for export or settings; export runs in the inspector, settings is a page.
**Don't** animate on launch, block input during a transition, or use bounce, overshoot or springs.
**Don't** use the day-to-night ramp in chrome or text, or any text grey lighter than Ink Secondary.
**Don't** use emoji, gradient text, side-stripe borders or decorative glass.
